subject: Biology
objectiveMappingPolicy: Official objectives are retained at topic level because the cited KIE syllabuses do not map each objective one-to-one to a numbered sub-topic.

source.authority: Kenya Institute of Education (KIE), Ministry of Education, Science and Technology
source.title: Secondary Education Syllabus Volume Two

objectives.label: a)
objectives.text: define transport and explain the necessity of transport in plants and animals

objectives.label: b)
objectives.text: relate the structure of the root, root hair, xylem and phloem to their functions

objectives.label: c)
objectives.text: relate the internal structure of the leaf to transpiration

objectives.label: d)
objectives.text: explain possible forces involved in the movement of water and mineral salts through the plant

objectives.label: e)
objectives.text: explain the significance of and factors affecting transpiration

objectives.label: f)
objectives.text: demonstrate simple experiments on transpiration

objectives.label: g)
objectives.text: distinguish between closed and open circulatory systems

objectives.label: h)
objectives.text: relate the structure of the heart and the blood vessels to their functions

objectives.label: i)
objectives.text: trace the path taken by blood from the heart to all parts of the body, and back to the heart

objectives.label: j)
objectives.text: name the common diseases of the circulatory system in humans and suggest methods of control / prevention

objectives.label: k)
objectives.text: relate the structure of the components of blood to their functions

objectives.label: l)
objectives.text: explain how oxygen and carbon dioxide are transported in the blood

objectives.label: m)
objectives.text: describe the mechanism of blood clotting and its importance

objectives.label: n)
objectives.text: describe the human blood groups and their importance in blood transfusion

objectives.label: o)
objectives.text: explain immunity and describe immune responses.

Absorption of Water and Mineral Salts
Transpiration
Translocation

objectives.label: a)
objectives.text: explain the need for gaseous exchange in living organisms

objectives.label: b)
objectives.text: explain the mechanism of gaseous exchange in plants

objectives.label: c)
objectives.text: compare the internal structures of aquatic and terrestrial roots, stems and leaves

objectives.label: d)
objectives.text: examine various types of respiratory structures in animals and relate them to their functions

objectives.label: e)
objectives.text: state the characteristics of respiratory surfaces

objectives.label: f)
objectives.text: describe the mechanisms of gaseous exchange in protozoa, insects, fish, frog and mammal

objectives.label: g)
objectives.text: describe the factors which control the rate of breathing in humans

objectives.label: h)
objectives.text: state the causes, symptoms and prevention of respiratory diseases.

subTopics.name: Gaseous exchange in living organisms (necessity)
Gaseous Exchange in Plants
Gaseous Exchange in Animals
Factors affecting rate of breathing in humans
Respiratory diseases: Asthma, Bronchitis, Pulmonary tuberculosis, Pneumonia and Whooping cough

objectives.label: a)
objectives.text: explain the significance of respiration in living organisms

objectives.label: b)
objectives.text: distinguish between aerobic and anaerobic respiration

objectives.label: c)
objectives.text: describe the economic importance of anaerobic respiration in industry and at home

objectives.label: d)
objectives.text: describe experiments to show that respiration takes place in plants and animals.86

subTopics.name: Meaning and significance of respiration
Tissue respiration

objectives.label: a)
objectives.text: distinguish between excretion and egestion

objectives.label: b)
objectives.text: explain the necessity for excretion in plants and animals

objectives.label: c)
objectives.text: state the uses of excretory products of plants

objectives.label: d)
objectives.text: describe the methods of excretion in a named unicellular organism

objectives.label: e)
objectives.text: relate the structures of the human skin, lungs, liver and kidney to their functions

objectives.label: f)
objectives.text: name common kidney diseases

objectives.label: g)
objectives.text: explain the concept of internal environment and homeostasis

objectives.label: h)
objectives.text: compare responses to changes in temperature by behavioural and physiological methods in animals

objectives.label: i)
objectives.text: relate heat loss to body size in mammals

objectives.label: j)
objectives.text: describe methods by which mammals gain and lose heat

objectives.label: k)
objectives.text: explain how the functions of the following relate to homeostasis - skin, hypothalamus, liver and kidney

objectives.label: l)
objectives.text: discuss the role of antidiuretic hormone, insulin and glucagons

objectives.label: m)
objectives.text: describe simple symptoms of Diabetes mellitus and Diabetes insipidus.
